Outbreak of Norovirus Hits Farm Workers in Southern Ontario, Disrupting Harvests

A sudden outbreak of norovirus among farm workers in the Leamington region of southern Ontario is causing significant disruption to this season’s vegetable harvest, according to local agricultural representatives and health officials. 

The outbreak, which began last week, has primarily affected workers at multiple greenhouse and field sites, including those operated by Green Valley Produce and Suncrest Farms. As of Wednesday, the Essex County Agricultural Health Unit confirmed more than 120 reported cases of illness among farm workers, with symptoms including vomiting, diarrhea, and fever.

"We are doing everything possible to contain the spread," said Maria Lopez, spokesperson for Green Valley Produce. "However, with so many workers off sick, we’ve had to temporarily halt operations in several greenhouses and delay field picking schedules."

The Leamington Growers’ Association estimates that up to 25% of the local seasonal workforce is currently unable to work, leading to concerns over crop losses and unharvested produce. "The labour shortage is making it hard to keep up with the perishable crop schedule," explained association chair Peter Sutherland. "We’re prioritizing high-value crops but expect to lose some yield if the situation doesn’t improve soon."

Affected sites have implemented enhanced sanitation protocols and staggered shifts to help contain the virus. "Our first priority is the health of our workers," said Suncrest Farms manager Felicia Chen. "We’re working closely with health authorities and following all recommended guidelines."

Local health officials continue to monitor the situation, urging workers and farm operators to remain vigilant, as the outbreak remains ongoing.
